name: Politics
dimension: the aspect of power the claim concerns

objects.label: Authority
objects.text: PO.O.A1 Authority

objects.label: States and sovereignty
objects.text: PO.O.A1.1 States and sovereignty — Weber's state: a community that successfully claims a monopoly of legitimate force in a territory.

objects.label: Legitimacy as belief
objects.text: PO.O.A1.2 Legitimacy as belief — measured acceptance of a ruler's right. Whether the rule is justified is PL.

objects.label: Regimes
objects.text: PO.O.A1.3 Regimes — democracy, autocracy, hybrid regimes, classified by stated criteria (V-Dem, Polity: W12 for coding rules).

objects.label: Institutions
objects.text: PO.O.A2 Institutions

objects.label: Constitutional design
objects.text: PO.O.A2.1 Constitutional design — presidential and parliamentary systems, federalism. The legal text is LA; its political effect is PO.

objects.label: Electoral systems
objects.text: PO.O.A2.2 Electoral systems — Duverger's law: plurality rule in single-member districts tends toward two-party competition. It is a tendency with known exceptions (e.g. India, Canada).

objects.label: Parties
objects.text: PO.O.A2.3 Parties — party systems, organisation, cleavages.

objects.label: Legislatures and executives
objects.text: PO.O.A2.4 Legislatures and executives — veto players: policy stability rises with the number and ideological distance of veto players (Tsebelis).

objects.label: Selectorate theory
objects.text: PO.O.A2.5 Selectorate theory — leaders keep office by rewarding a winning coalition W drawn from a selectorate S. When W is small relative to S, leaders favour private goods over public ones (Bueno de Mesquita et al., 2003).

objects.label: Political behaviour
objects.text: PO.O.A3 Political behaviour

objects.label: Voting (median voter)
objects.text: PO.O.A3.1 Voting — the median voter theorem: with one policy dimension, single-peaked preferences and majority rule, the median voter's ideal point beats any other. Theorem MA.B.C4; use PO.

objects.label: Public opinion
objects.text: PO.O.A3.2 Public opinion — attitudes measured by survey. The cognitive mechanism is MS.

objects.label: Participation and movements
objects.text: PO.O.A3.3 Participation and social movements — turnout, collective action. Olson: large groups under-provide collective goods without selective incentives.

objects.label: Conflict within states
objects.text: PO.O.A3.4 Conflict within states — civil war onset, coups, revolution. The conduct of the fighting is ST.

objects.label: Policy and administration
objects.text: PO.O.A4 Policy and administration

objects.label: Agenda and decision
objects.text: PO.O.A4.1 Agenda and decision — punctuated equilibrium; the multiple streams model (a framework, W9).

objects.label: Bureaucracy
objects.text: PO.O.A4.2 Bureaucracy — delegation, principal–agent control (theory EC.O.A2.3).

objects.label: Implementation
objects.text: PO.O.A4.3 Implementation — the gap between decision and delivery.

objects.label: Policy effects
objects.text: PO.O.A4.4 Policy effects — the causal effect of a policy is owned by the field of the outcome (EC, MD, ED), and PO cites it. The political cause of the policy is PO.

objects.label: Relations among states
objects.text: PO.O.A5 Relations among states

objects.label: International order
objects.text: PO.O.A5.1 International order — anarchy, balance of power, hegemony. Realist, liberal and constructivist claims are competing programmes (CONTESTED).

objects.label: Cooperation and institutions
objects.text: PO.O.A5.2 Cooperation and international institutions — regimes, alliances, the UN. The treaty's legal force is LA.

objects.label: War and peace
objects.text: PO.O.A5.3 War and peace — the democratic peace: pairs of democracies rarely fight each other. It is an empirical regularity; its causes are CONTESTED. The strategy of coercion and conduct is ST.

warrants.standard: identified effect of a rule; formal result; cases
survey with stated error; experiment; identified effect

sections.governing_thought:
Politics is exhausted by four faces of one pyramid: objects, methods, warrants and bridges.
Its objects divide into five aspects of power: authority, institutions, political behaviour, policy and administration, and relations among states.
sections.key_line:
Dimension: **the aspect of power the claim concerns.** Order: from the source of authority outward.
1. Authority
2. Institutions
3. Political behaviour
4. Policy and administration
5. Relations among states
sections.assignment_rules:
1. Place an empirical claim by the aspect of power.
2. Whether rule is justified is PL; whether people believe it is justified is PO.
3. Legal validity is LA; the political cause or effect of a law is PO.
4. The policy's causal effect belongs to its outcome field; its political origin is PO.
5. The conduct of war, coercion and the choice of game are ST; war onset and the international order are PO.
6. The theorem is MA; its political use is PO.
7. A dated political event is HI; its explanation is PO.
